title: '6-to-1' Shopping Method Could Help You Save Money
paragraphs: Do you often spend too much money at the supermarket, or throw away food that you forgot to eat? If so, a shopping method called "6-to-1" might help.

The method was created by Will Coleman, a food content creator and recipe developer based in Brooklyn, New York. It has become popular on social media sites such as TikTok and Instagram. Coleman said that he created it because he wanted to take control of his money and his time.

The idea is simple. Once a week, you go to the store and buy six vegetables, five fruits, four sources of protein, three starches, two sauces or spreads and one fun item just for yourself. People with large families may want to go shopping twice a week.

Coleman says that vegetables can include basic items such as onions and garlic, which he uses in almost every meal. People can also buy vegetables that are on sale, and they can choose canned or frozen fruit and vegetables if fresh ones are too expensive or out of season. The fun item can be any treat that you enjoy.

According to Coleman, the method has saved him hundreds of dollars. One reason is that having a plan stops him from buying things that he will not use. He also says that he does not throw food away, because he knows what is in his fridge and what meals he will make with it. To make planning easier, he suggests deciding on a few meals for the week, such as pasta or a salad.
Coleman says the method has also saved him a lot of time, because he spends less time deciding what to buy and cook.
However, there have been no scientific studies on how much money the method saves. Most of the evidence comes from people's own experiences.
